title: T22 (Tinyana) PNC - True Humility Requires Daas — Flattery Disguised as Anavah
author: Pettek Nanach

beginner.en: Most people misread humility. We labor in service and prayer to climb out of mochin de-katnus (small consciousness) into mochin de-gadlus (expansive consciousness). If 'humility' meant simply collapsing oneself, it would drag you straight back into katnus. So real anavah requires daas — judgment about when to bend and when to stand. Only Moshe achieved 'most humble of all men.' Humility without daas is what Chazal call chanufah (flattery): Yirmiyahu's 'Amen' to the false prophet Chananyah was that kind of bowing, and the Gemara says all flatterers fall into their son's hand.

intermediate.en: Hachna'ah ke-ra'uy demands daas because hishtaplus without daas is functionally chanufah toward whomever is in front of you. Moshe rabbeinu, anav mi-kol ha-adam (Bamidbar 12:3), held humility together with Sotah 41b's warning. Cf. Tinyana T14 (adversaries above mirror those below) — false-humility is the lower face of false-mefursamim. The PNC reading: chanufah masquerading as anavah is the most patient of nivla — it preserves the falseness it bows to. Practical: if your 'humility' is silencing rebuke that should be spoken, suspect chanufah.
